description: Tellstone is a high-performance in-memory database and drop-in replacement for Redis; Join https://discord.gg/kEf78DUFX

summary.one_liner: Tellstone is an in-memory key/value store written in Go that serves a custom binary protocol and a Redis-compatible (RESP2) listener from a shared-nothing sharded engine.
summary.what_it_does: Tellstone stores keys and values in memory across N shards, each holding a map and a read-write lock, with keys assigned to shards by FNV-1a hash. It exposes a native binary protocol on port 9988 with a bundled Go client, and an optional RESP2 listener (port 6379) that supports PING, GET, SET (with EX/PX), DEL, AUTH, COMMAND, ROLE and ACL commands. Expired keys are evicted actively by a timing wheel and lazily on read. Optional features include ChaCha20-Poly1305 at-rest encryption, per-shard write-ahead log persistence with snapshots, TLS with certificate rotation, password or RBAC-based authentication, and OAuth/OIDC token login. It also provides a Prometheus metrics exporter, optional OpenTelemetry tracing, and structured JSON audit logging.
use_cases: replace Redis as a drop-in cache for existing clients
session or token storage in memory
benchmarking in-memory stores against Redis, Valkey or Dragonfly
running a small in-memory store on Kubernetes
notable: Serves both a custom binary protocol and a Redis-compatible RESP2 listener on the same engine
Shared-nothing sharded design with per-shard locks and FNV-1a dispatch
Per-shard append-only WAL with tombstone deletes, disabled by default
Automatic TLS certificate rotation via directory watching, plus optional STARTTLS on the RESP listener
RBAC policy file with bcrypt passwords, hot-reloaded on SIGHUP, and OAuth/OIDC federated login
caveats: Supported Redis commands are limited to PING, GET, SET, DEL, AUTH, COMMAND, ROLE and ACL; the README says replication and broader RESP coverage are still contribution areas
Benchmark numbers are self-reported by the project and depend heavily on hardware and network setup; the README notes results are environment-specific
Requires Go 1.26+ to build from source; the README does not list other platform constraints beyond Linux, macOS and Windows binaries
Encryption key must be supplied explicitly when encryption is enabled, and rotating it requires a restart
